recommendation_summary: The reply recommends a hosted dead-man heartbeat: keep cron on edna, have the script send a success ping when it finishes and a fail ping on a nonzero exit, and have the host message the user if the success ping hasn't arrived by 04:30.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked to know by morning if nightly-sync failed or never finished, without reading logs.
labels.Deleted: Central log on Synology and moving everything to Docker, both suggested by you, because a log you will not read would not have alerted on those four silent nights and adds a second system to maintain for one cron job.
labels.Bottleneck: The email only sends on the success path, so a startup crash is silent and nothing checks for absence.
labels.Checked myself: You told me nightly-sync is the only job, cron on edna at 03:00, email on finish, expired token killed it four nights before email, nothing else alerts, and you will not read logs.

note: The reply recommends one hosted heartbeat alert, and its four labelled lines come first, rule out the user's Synology and Docker idea, and cite only facts the user gave.
